name: Lydmouth Town

location.about: A port of about 230,000 where the River Lyd meets the sea, twenty miles downstream from Kingsmere: docks, ferries, cruise ships and the navy. A working town that looks down on the cathedral city up the river - and the most up-and-down club in England.

colours.story: Yellow and royal blue - the colours of the Lydmouth harbour pilots' flag. The club was started by pilots and dockers in 1876.

home.shirt: yellow with royal-blue collar and cuffs

third.shirt: white with a yellow and blue band across the chest

rivals.why: the cathedral city twenty miles up the river - coast against city since 1882
the 12-1 in the Association Cup of 1886, still the club's record defeat

history.title: The pilots' club
history.text: Founded in 1876 by harbour pilots and dockers. Association Cup finals lost in 1880 and 1889 (and a 12-1 defeat at Bramhall in 1886); promoted to the top division in 1894 - and the Association Cup at last in 1914.

history.title: The best years
history.text: Second in the League in 1936 and the Association Cup in 1935 - then, in 1950, champions of England, the only title in the club's history. Relegated three years later; back as Second Division champions in 1955.

history.title: Giant-killers
history.text: Down again in the sixties - and in 1969 they won the Association Cup as a Second Division club, and the Second Division too. The League Cup in 1975 (another Second Division season, promoted as runners-up), relegated, and back as champions in 1978.

history.title: The yo-yo
history.text: Second in the League in 1987; down; back through the play-offs in 1990; down; up again in 1993, 2001 and 2005. No club has gone up and down more.

history.title: Play-off specialists
history.text: Relegated again in the 2010s, promoted through the play-offs in 2019; an Association Cup final in 2020; down; and up through the play-offs once more in 2024 - three play-off finals, three wins.

history.title: The season of their lives
history.text: Two years after coming up, Lydmouth finished second in the League in 2026 - their best season since 1950. The same spring Kingsmere won the Association Cup. The Hampshire Derby has never been bigger.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1950 = 1949-50).

legends.name: Captain Harry Doust
legends.note: The club's first captain and chairman. The Pilots' Bar is in his old house.

legends.name: Reg Cobb
legends.note: The 1950 title. The Cobb Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Micky Shaw
legends.note: 707 appearances - the club record; kept goal in the 1969 cup final.

legends.name: Dave Penfold
legends.note: The 2019 play-off final and the 2020 cup final.

legends.name: Theo Marsh-Adeyemi
legends.note: The goals of the 2024 promotion and the 2026 runners-up.

records.attendance: 51,370 v Kingsmere City, League, 1950 (Harbour Road, before seating)

badge.about: The lighthouse at the harbour mouth and the pilot's flag; the waves of the Lyd. Motto 'Lumen in Undis' - a light on the waves.
badge.design: A royal-blue shield with a yellow border. In the centre a white lighthouse with a yellow lamp shining two beams, standing on rocks above three wavy yellow lines. A small yellow-and-blue pilot's flag flying from the lighthouse. 'LYDMOUTH TOWN' arched above the shield in royal-blue capitals, and a yellow ribbon beneath reading 'LUMEN IN UNDIS' in royal blue, with '1876' on the ribbon's ends.

ground.name: Harbour Road

stands.name: Cobb Stand
stands.features: the main stand: tunnel, dugouts, a row of boxes; Reg Cobb's statue outside

stands.name: Quay End
stands.features: the home end - one steep single tier in yellow seats, the cranes of the container port behind it

stands.name: Pilots' Stand
stands.features: the oldest stand - wooden seats long gone, a few pillars still in the way; the club wants to rebuild it

stands.name: Town End
stands.features: away fans; the old town and the ferry terminal behind it

ground.roof: four separate roofs, the Pilots' Stand's held up on pillars
ground.surroundings: the docks and container cranes behind the Quay End, ferries and a lighthouse at the harbour mouth, the old town's narrow streets to the north
ground.atmosphere: a small, tight, loud ground by the sea - and full every week since 2024
